## ECR Club — Next Session (9 Dec)

::: section
![](https://thieled.github.io/ecpr-newsletter/assets/banners/ecr_club_sq.png){.newsimg width="180"}

The PolComm ECR Club is pleased to announce its next online session featuring **Roy Aulie Jacobsen** and his paper *“An Emotional Reaction: Analysing the Public’s Response to Communication Tactics Used by Political Leaders in Norway during the COVID-19 Pandemic”.* 
The study explores how different communication strategies on Facebook trigger emotional reactions and shape public engagement during the pandemic.

The PolComm ECR Club is a monthly forum open to PhD students and postdocs (≤4 years post-PhD) in the ECPR or ECREA political communication sections.

**Time:** Tuesday 11:00 - 12:00 GMT (09/12/2025)  \
**Presenter:** Roy Aulie Jacobsen, Kristiania University Oslo  \
**Discussant:** Pablo Jost, University of Mainz \
**Chair:** Nicoleta Corbu, SNSPA, Bucharest \

<button class="readmore">
<a href="https://ecpr.eu/Events/332">Read more</a>
</button>
:::


## Call for Papers — ECPR Joint Sessions 2026

::: section

We are pleased to share that the PolComm Standing Group is endorsing the workshop *“The Rise of Hostile Communication Styles and their Consequences for the Functioning of Modern Democracies”* at the **ECPR Joint Sessions** of Workshops 2026, taking place 7–10 April at the University of Innsbruck.

Chaired by Jeremy Dodeigne (University of Namur) and Chiara Vargiu (University of Amsterdam), this workshop explores the evolution and effects of hostile political rhetoric—beyond polarization—on democratic systems. It invites conceptual innovation and comparative empirical work, especially on how institutional contexts shape elite hostility and its impact on turnout, trust, and political stability.

The call for papers is now open. **Deadline:** 3 December 2025.

<button class="readmore"> <a href="https://ecpr.eu/Events/Event/Content?ID=1555&EventID=342">Submit your paper</a> </button> 

:::

## General Conference 2026 — Call for Papers

::: section

![](https://thieled.github.io/ecpr-newsletter/issues/2025/12/img/krakow_sq.png){.newsimg width="180"}

The PolComm Standing Group is proud to endorse the section *“Political Communication Between Disruptive Technologies and Democratic Backsliding”* at the **ECPR General Conference**, taking place 8–11 September 2026 at Jagiellonian University, Krakow.

Chaired by Johanna Burger, the section explores how political communication mediates the convergence of technological upheaval and democratic erosion. Topics range from generative AI, disinformation, and deepfakes to media trust, regulatory responses, and democratic resilience.

We invite submissions from across the methodological spectrum—experimental, qualitative, computational, or comparative. If your research interrogates the nexus of tech, media, and democracy, this is your platform.

**Submission deadline:** 5 January 2026.

<button class="readmore"> <a href="https://ecpr.eu/Events/Event/SectionDetails/1677">Submit your paper</a> </button> 

:::
